subject: Citizenship

source.title: National curriculum in England: citizenship programmes of study for key stages 3 and 4

statementPolicy: Controlled paraphrases of the statutory programme of study, not verbatim curriculum text. Example content shown in square brackets and other non-statutory material are not treated as statutory objectives.

KS3: Law, justice and the legal system
Public institutions, voluntary groups and community participation
Research, evidence, debate and informed action
KS4: Parliamentary democracy and the UK constitution
Forms of government and international governance
UK law and the justice system
Identity, diversity, mutual respect and understanding
Research, evidence, persuasion and civic action

KS3.summary: Understand the development and operation of democratic government in the United Kingdom and the roles of citizens, Parliament and the monarch.
Understand how Parliament operates, including voting and elections, and understand the role of political parties.
Develop knowledge and understanding of the liberties and responsibilities associated with citizenship in the United Kingdom.

KS3.domain: Law, justice and the legal system
KS3.summary: Understand the nature of rules and laws and the operation of the justice system, including the roles of police, courts and tribunals.

KS3.domain: Public institutions, voluntary groups and community participation
KS3.summary: Understand the roles of public institutions and voluntary groups and ways citizens can work together to improve their communities.
Understand the functions and uses of money, the importance and practice of budgeting, and how to manage financial risk.

KS3.domain: Research, evidence, debate and informed action
KS3.summary: Research and interrogate evidence, debate and evaluate viewpoints, present reasoned arguments and take informed action.

KS4.domain: Parliamentary democracy and the UK constitution
KS4.summary: Understand parliamentary democracy and key elements of the UK constitution, including government power and the roles of the executive, legislature, judiciary, citizens and a free press.
Understand electoral systems and ways citizens can participate in democratic and electoral processes to influence decisions at different levels.

KS4.domain: Forms of government and international governance
KS4.summary: Understand different democratic and non-democratic systems of government and the UK's relationships with European, Commonwealth, United Nations and wider international institutions.
Develop knowledge and understanding of human rights and international law.

KS4.domain: UK law and the justice system
KS4.summary: Understand the UK legal system, different sources of law and how law helps society respond to complex problems.

KS4.domain: Identity, diversity, mutual respect and understanding
KS4.summary: Understand diverse national, regional, religious and ethnic identities in the United Kingdom and the importance of mutual respect and understanding.
Understand ways citizens can contribute to improving their communities through volunteering and other responsible activity.
Understand income and expenditure, credit and debt, insurance, savings and pensions, financial products and services, and how public money is raised and spent.

KS4.domain: Research, evidence, persuasion and civic action
KS4.summary: Use research strategies, weigh evidence, make persuasive arguments, substantiate conclusions and evaluate ways citizens can act together to solve problems and contribute to society.
